entities.summary: Oswine of Kent was a 7th-century Anglo-Saxon king of Kent, reigning jointly with Swæfberht and Swæfheard from 688 till 690. He played a crucial role in the politics of Kent during the Early Medieval period, navigating the complex web of alliances and power struggles between the various Anglo-Saxon kingdoms. Oswine's reign was marked by the rise of Christianity in Kent, as he sought to strengthen his kingdom's position through strategic marriages and alliances with other Christian kingdoms. His legacy extended beyond his own reign, as his successors continued to navigate the treacherous landscape of Anglo-Saxon politics. Oswine's story serves as a microcosm of the complex and often brutal world of early medieval politics, where personal ambition, loyalty, and religious conviction often clashed in a delicate dance of power and survival.
